title: What is known about 1RB1RE_1LC0RA_1LD1LB_1LE0LF_1LA0LB_1LB---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RE_1LC0RA_1LD1LB_1LE0LF_1LA0LB_1LB---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. At a right turn the tape is a word over 100, 10 and 10000 (at a left turn: blocks of 5 and 7 ones and the group 2 6 9). All of it except a zone at the left end slides 9 cells to the right per round trip; the right end consumes the last run of 100s, two per round trip. The left zone acts like a counter: usually a few hundred cells, it sometimes reaches thousands (carries). The sweep rules are proved in Lean.
Lean proves no halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps (10,000 by the kernel alone); the C simulator finds none in 10<sup>9</sup>.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 74,437 cells have been visited and 32,906 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: sqrt/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.484). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.522).

claims.title: The sweep rules
claims.text: Shift rules of the two sweeps, for every repeat count and any tape around: going right A turns each 111 into 010 and B each block 110111 into 001001; going left B turns each 010010 back into 111011.

claims.title: A conveyor
claims.text: Compared with the previous left turn, all of the tape but a zone at the left end is the old tape moved 9 cells right (cells 47..3,187 of 3,187 at 2.4·10<sup>6</sup> steps).

claims.title: The left engine
claims.text: The changing zone at the left end is 31 to 6,431 cells wide over the first 3·10<sup>9</sup> steps, usually a few hundred: it behaves like a counter with occasional long carries.

claims.title: The reader at the right end
claims.text: At a right turn the tape ends with a run (100)^k and k drops by 1 per right turn (2 per round trip); when it runs out, the next marker 10000 and the run before it take its place.

claims.title: The halt needs 1 D>1
claims.text: The only halting transition F1 is reached only from 1 D>1. In the first 109 steps D reads a 1 53,174,798 times, never with a 1 on its left.

claims.title: The mirrored table of 1RB0RC_1LC1LA, a different start
claims.text: Mirroring left and right and renaming the states A, B, C, D, E, F of this machine to B, C, D, E, A, F gives the transition table of 1RB0RC_1LC1LA_1RD0LB_1RE1RC_1RA0RF_1RC--- exactly (proved in lean/Twin.lean: the renaming commutes with every step, and halts_iff says this machine halts from blank tape exactly when that table halts from the other start). So this machine started on blank tape runs like the mirror image of that one started in state B instead of A. The shared table does not make the halting questions the same. The two machines start from different configurations, and their runs from blank tape never reach a common configuration (checked for the first 200,000 steps, up to the renaming). So one could halt and the other not; each is its own open question.
claims.where: lean/Twin.lean (step_tw, init_eq, halts_iff); the runs compared by py/compare_starts.py in the folder of 1RB0RC_1LC1LA

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The right-end reader looks like a simple finite process on the runs it eats; the left engine is a counter-like zone whose output is not understood. A proof would describe both and show that the reader never meets a word that halts.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 74,437 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.484). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.522).
After 109 steps the tape spans 74,437 cells (46,066 left of the start, 8,072 right), with a density of 1s of 0.442.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: A conveyor belt
html: At a right turn the tape reads like (100)^7 10000 (100)^5 10000 (100)^15 … 10000 (100)^104: runs of 100 separated by markers 10000, plus 10s near the left end. The belt moves 9 cells right per round trip. The rightmost run shrinks by two 100s per round trip.

sections.heading: Rules proved in Lean
html:
rulefromtowhat it does
a_111L A> (111)^n RL (010)^n A> RRightward: A turns each 111 into 010.
b_blockL B> (110111)^n RL (001001)^n B> RRightward: B turns each 110111 (a block of five ones and its 0) into 001001.
b_unblockL (010010)^n B> 0 RL B> 0 (111011)^n RLeftward: B turns each 010010 back into 111011.
A block 1^5 0 at a left turn is (100)^2 at a right turn: b_block converts one way, b_unblock the other.

sections.heading: Where a halt would come from
html: It halts from 1 D>1; D reads a 1 about 53 million times in 109 steps, always with a 0 on its left. Both the engine and the reader would have to be understood to rule it out.

summary: A conveyor: a counter-like engine at the left end writes words that ride right 9 cells per round trip, and the right end eats them, shortening the last run by 2 words per round trip.
family: conveyor between a left engine and a right-end reader

sections.heading: How it works
paragraphs: The tape is a conveyor belt. At a right turn it is a word over 100, 10 and the marker 10000. Each round trip, everything except a zone at the left end slides 9 cells to the right, unchanged. The zone at the left end is an engine that writes new words onto the belt; it behaves like a counter, usually a few hundred cells wide but sometimes rewriting thousands (a long carry).

At the right end the machine eats the belt: the last run of 100s shrinks by two words per round trip, and when it is used up the next marker and run take its place. A halt needs 1 D>1, which never happened in 109 steps.
